data.paraphrase: For every natural number n ≥ 1995, the number of matrices M in SM(n) where the row sums of M are three consecutive integers is at least four times the number of matrices M in SM(n) where all row sums of M are equal. This holds under the conditions that SM(n) consists of all 3×n matrices with integer entries where each column sums to exactly {1, 2, 3}, and Srowsums(n, M) yields the set of row sums of M. Additionally, sumsprog(S) is true if and only if S has exactly three elements that are consecutive integers starting from some integer a, and b = a + 1, c = a + 2 for some integers a, b, c in S.
